newsitem.title: UK: UK bank lending grows 8.214 billion stg in Q3 - BBA.
newsitem.headline: UK bank lending grows 8.214 billion stg in Q3 - BBA.

text.p: Total lending of the Major British Banking Groups (MBBG) increased by 8.214 billion stg in the three months to the end of September, the British Bankers Association said on Tuesday.
This compared with a revised figure of 10.225 billion stg in the second quarter.

"The increase in consumer credit of over 1.30 billion stg was a record for the MBBG series," Tim Sweeney, director general of the BBA, said in a statement. "Overall however, the pace of growth in the major banks' lending slowed somewhat in the third quarter of the year."
The analysis of lending showed individuals and financial companies accounted for virtually all the increase in identified lending.

Personal borrowing rose by 2.937 billion stg (1.6 percent) almost exactly the same as in the second quarter, while consumer credit increased by 1.353 billion stg (3.5 percent) for the second quarter in succession, the largest increase since the series began in 1991.
"Growth in lending to financial companies, though smaller than in the second quarter, was again substantial," Sweeney said.
Lending to industrial and commercial companies, which had risen significantly in each of the six previous quarters, was essentially unchanged over the period.
Mortgage lending rose by 1.614 billion stg (up 1.1 percent) which was down somewhat compared with the rise in the first two quarters.
